1.q: כִּי־יִמָּצֵ֣א חָלָ֗ל בָּ⁠אֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜י⁠ךָ נֹתֵ֤ן לְ⁠ךָ֙ לְ⁠רִשְׁתָּ֔⁠הּ נֹפֵ֖ל בַּ⁠שָּׂדֶ֑ה לֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע מִ֥י הִכָּֽה⁠וּ
1.note: Moses is describing a possible condition in which someone is found murdered and the killer is unknown. The instructions for what they should do if this situation occurs is described in verses 2–9. Express this possible condition in a way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Suppose someone is found murdered in the land that Yahweh your God is giving you to possess, lying in a field, and no one knows who killed him]

The expression **is found** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [If someone finds a dead person]
See how you translated the phrase “Yahweh your God” in 1:10.

The expression **it is not known** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one knows who killed him] or [and you cannot identify who attacked him]

2.note: Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and they shall measure the distance from where the body was found to the cities]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. The same occurs in the next verse. Alternate translation: [the slain person’s body] or [the location where the murdered person was found]

3.note: The expression **has not been put to work** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a heifer of the herd, one that no one has ever used for work]

4.q: אֵיתָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־יֵעָבֵ֥ד בּ֖⁠וֹ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יִזָּרֵ֑עַ
4.note: This describes a place that should be completely natural and untouched by human cultivation. This symbolizes innocence and purity in this ritual for dealing with an unresolved murder. You may want to explain this symbolism in a footnote.

The expression **that has not been worked in, nor sown** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [where no one has ever plowed or planted seeds]

Breaking the neck of a heifer was a symbolic action that showed that the community was dealing with the guilt of an unsolved murder even though they were not responsible for it. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and there in the valley the elders shall break the neck of the heifer to show that they are free from guilt for the murder]

5.note: The phrases **the priests** and **the sons of Levi** mean similar things. Moses is using the two phrases together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the Levitical priests]
Alternate translation: [And … must come to the valley]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

Even though Moses is speaking to a group of people, the Israelites, **your** is singular in this verse. If the singular forms of this pronoun would not be natural in your language, you could use the plural form in your translation.

Here, **in the name of Yahweh** represents “with Yahweh’s authority.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with Yahweh’s authority and as his representatives]

Here, **mouth** represents “authority.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and they have the authority to make decisions about every dispute and case of assault]

6.note: The elders washing their hands over the heifer was a symbolic action that showed they were declaring their innocence in the death of the murdered person. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [shall, in order to declare their innocence, wash their hands over the heifer]

The expression **was broken** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the heifer whose neck the elders broke]

7.note: Here the elders are responding to a situation, not to something that someone said. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall say in response to the murder situation]

The term **and say** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly. Alternate translation: [and they shall respond] or [and they shall answer]

The elders are using one part of their bodies **Our hands**, to mean all of them in the act of spilling the blood. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [We have not spilled this blood]

Here the phrase **spilled this blood** is being used as a common expression of this culture to mean “kill this person.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Our hands have not killed this person]

The elders are using one part of their bodies **our eyes**, to mean all of them in the act of seeing the murder. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [nor have we seen it]

The elders are leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [have not seen it happen] or [have not seen who killed this person]

8.note: Here the elders are speaking as if Yahweh could literally **Cover** his people Israel. They are asking God to protect his people from guilt. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Forgive] or [Show mercy to]

8.q: וְ⁠אַל־תִּתֵּן֙ דָּ֣ם נָקִ֔י בְּ⁠קֶ֖רֶב עַמְּ⁠ךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
8.note: The speakers are using **put the blood of the innocent in the midst of your people Israel** as a common expression of their culture to mean “hold your people responsible for the murder of an innocent person.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not hold your people Israel accountable for the death of this innocent person] or [and do not charge your people Israel with the guilt of this murder]

Moses is using the adjective **innocent** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the blood of the person who has not done anything wrong]

The expression **be covered** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Then Yahweh will cover the guilt of this bloodshed and forgive his people] or [Then Yahweh will remove their guilt for this death]

Here Moses is speaking as if the guilt of shedding **blood** were actually something that could be **covered**. This refers to the guilt of bloodshed being forgiven or hidden from sight. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they will be forgiven for the death of this person] or [And Yahweh will remove their guilt for this bloodshed]

9.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **right**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when you do what Yahweh considers righteous]
See how you translated the phrase “in the eyes of” in 4:25. Alternate translation: [what is right in Yahweh’s judgment]

10.note: Here Moses is speaking as if the enemies were actually objects which could be placed **into your hands**. This expression represents God giving the Israelites victory over their enemies. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly as modeled by the UST.

In this verse, the word **captive** is singular in form, but it refers to all the enemies as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form. Alternate translation: [and you take its captives captive]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **captive**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and you take them away as people you have captured]

12.note: The instructions to **shave her head and do her nails** was a symbolic action that showed a transition from her prior identity to her new status, and was also part of mourning practices. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And she shall shave her head and trim her nails as part of her mourning and transition to her new life]

13.note: Moses is referring to sexual intimacy in a polite way by using the phrase **go in to her**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [you shall become intimate with her] or [you shall have sexual relations with her]

14.note: The implication is that the man has already humiliated the woman by taking her captive, making her change her appearance and identity, having sexual relations with her, and then rejecting her. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in return for having already humiliated her by taking her captive, changing her identity, and then rejecting her]

15.q: כִּֽי־תִהְיֶ֨יןָ לְ⁠אִ֜ישׁ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֗ים הָ⁠אַחַ֤ת אֲהוּבָה֙ וְ⁠הָ⁠אַחַ֣ת שְׂנוּאָ֔ה וְ⁠יָֽלְדוּ־ל֣⁠וֹ בָנִ֔ים הָ⁠אֲהוּבָ֖ה וְ⁠הַ⁠שְּׂנוּאָ֑ה וְ⁠הָיָ֛ה הַ⁠בֵּ֥ן הַ⁠בְּכ֖וֹר לַ⁠שְּׂנִיאָֽה
15.note: Moses is describing a possible condition in which the events in verse 16 will take place only if a man has two wives and the firstborn son belongs to the wife he does not love. Express this possible condition in a way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Suppose a man has two wives, one whom he loves and one whom he does not love, and both have given him sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the wife he does not love]

The terms **loved** and **hated** are passive verbal forms. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the man loves one wife more than he loves the other wife]

15.q: הָ⁠אֲהוּבָ֖ה וְ⁠הַ⁠שְּׂנוּאָ֑ה וְ⁠הָיָ֛ה הַ⁠בֵּ֥ן הַ⁠בְּכ֖וֹר לַ⁠שְּׂנִיאָֽה
15.note: Moses is using the adjectives **loved** and **hated** as nouns to mean certain kinds of wives. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [both the wife he loves and the wife he does not love, and if the firstborn son’s mother happens to be the wife he does not love]

16.note: Moses is using the adjective **beloved** as a noun to mean a certain kind of wife. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the son of the beloved wife]

Moses is using **upon the face of** as a common expression of his culture to mean “in preference to” or “instead of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [instead of the son of the wife he does not love] or [at the expense of the son of the wife he does not love]

Moses is using the adjective **hated** as a noun to mean a certain kind of wife. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. This phrase repeats in the next verse. Alternate translation: [the son of the wife he does not love]

17.note: The expression **is found** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a double portion of all that he owns]

By **the beginning of his strength**, Moses means the man’s first demonstration of his ability to father children. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers as modeled in the UST.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **regulation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [he has the legal rights that belong to a firstborn son] or [he is entitled to what the law requires for a firstborn son]

18.note: Moses is describing a possible condition of having a rebellious son. The instructions for what they should do in this situation is described in verses 19–21. Express this possible condition in a way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [If it should happen that a man has a stubborn and rebellious son]

18.q: אֵינֶ֣⁠נּוּ שֹׁמֵ֔עַ בְּ⁠ק֥וֹל & וְ⁠לֹ֥א יִשְׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵי⁠הֶֽם
18.note: Here Moses assumes that readers will know that the word translated as **listen** includes the meaning of “obey.” You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who will not obey the voice of … but he will not obey them]

18.q: אֵינֶ֣⁠נּוּ שֹׁמֵ֔עַ בְּ⁠ק֥וֹל אָבִ֖י⁠ו וּ⁠בְ⁠ק֣וֹל אִמּ֑⁠וֹ
18.note: Here, **the voice** represents the commands or instructions the parents give. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [who will not obey his parents’ instructions]

Moses uses the word **but** here to indicate a contrast between the parents’ discipline and the son’s continued disobedience. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and even though they discipline him, he still will not obey them]

20.q: וְ⁠אָמְר֞וּ אֶל־זִקְנֵ֣י עִיר֗⁠וֹ בְּנֵ֤⁠נוּ זֶה֙ סוֹרֵ֣ר וּ⁠מֹרֶ֔ה אֵינֶ֥⁠נּוּ שֹׁמֵ֖עַ בְּ⁠קֹלֵ֑⁠נוּ זוֹלֵ֖ל וְ⁠סֹבֵֽא
20.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Then the parents must explain to the elders of the city that their son is stubborn and rebellious, that he will not obey them, and that he is a glutton and a drunkard.]

Here, **our voice** represents the parents’ instructions or commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he will not obey our instructions]

21.note: See how you translated this same phrase in 13:5.

The words **And all Israel will hear and fear** indicate the result of executing the rebellious son. If it would be clearer in your language, you could make this logical relationship explicit. Alternate translation: [As a result, all Israel will hear about this punishment and be afraid to behave in the same way]

22.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgment**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a crime that requires the death penalty] or [an offense for which he deserves to die]

The expression **is put to death** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and you execute him] or [and you kill him]

23.q: לֹא־תָלִ֨ין נִבְלָת֜⁠וֹ עַל־הָ⁠עֵ֗ץ כִּֽי־קָב֤וֹר תִּקְבְּרֶ֨⁠נּוּ֙ בַּ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠ה֔וּא כִּֽי־קִלְלַ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים תָּל֑וּי
23.note: The word **for** indicates that what follows, **cursed of God is a hanged man**, is the reason for the command that came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases to put the reason before the command. Alternate translation: [because a hanged man is cursed by God, his corpse shall not remain on the tree. Instead, you shall surely bury him that day]

The expression **cursed of God** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God curses anyone who hangs on a tree]

23.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א תְטַמֵּא֙ אֶת־אַדְמָ֣תְ⁠ךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔י⁠ךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְ⁠ךָ֖ נַחֲלָֽה
23.note: Here Moses connects not leaving a corpse on a tree to not defiling the land that God is giving to the Israelites. This connection shows purpose or goal. In your language, you may need to express this relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [You must do this so that you do not defile the land that Yahweh your God is giving to you as an inheritance]
